newsitem.title: UK: Charts point to further lira weakness - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Charts point to further lira weakness - analysts.

text.p: The mark and dollar's clearance of key technical levels against the lira has hardened the view among chartists that lira weakness from its January highs is set to continue.

Tuesday's break above key resistance around the 992-993 lire area, the previous mark tops seen in early December and early February, is now expected to act as a base for further mark moves to the upside.

"The break above near-term resistance at the 992 area is quite key," said Ian Stannard, technical analyst at Chase Investment Bank in London. "If it holds above this level then the technical outlook improves for the mark."

The mark traded just shy of the key psychological barrier at 1000 lire, its next upside target, which is expected to prove a tough obstacle on its way to the next objective at 1012, the mark's high from November 1996.
"The 1000 level is clearly psychological, and at 1001 we have a 50 percent retracement of the move from 1037 to 965," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.
The mark touched a peak of 1037 in August 1996 before declining to its recent low around 966 in mid-January.
CSFB's Jones also identified a potential inverse head and shoulders, the head being the January low, a chart pattern which puts an upside target around 1021 lire.
Clearance of 1012, then 1021 sets up a medium-term target at the August high of 1037 lire.
On the downside, analysts were still cautious of a break below the 992-993 base.
"If it fails at 992, then mark/lira is more vulnerable to a dip back towards support at the 988-984 area," said Chase's Stannard. "Then we get trendline support from the January low at 979."
Against the dollar, the lira has sunk over 11 percent since January, with more dollar upside potential although analysts admit overbought conditions could weigh in the near-term.
"The break above the 1635 level takes us above a 14-year downtrend and it has broken out of channel resistance as well," said Stannard.

Today's dollar peak of 1687.90 takes it to levels not seen since May 1995 and, with long-term trend resistance broken, analysts are looking to peaks in this time period for the next upside objectives.
Above 1688, the next significant resistance is at the May 1995 high of 1706, which roughly coincides with a retracement level at 1710.
CSFB's Jones said 1710 is one of the more obscure Fibonacci retracements, being a 78.6 percent recovery of the dollar's downmove from its March 1995 peak of 1770 to the November 1996 low of 1488.
Above here, the March 1995 top is the medium-term objective.
On the downside, initial support lies at 1670 lire and then at around 1640, the previous long-term downtrend which also coincides with the uptrend from the January dollar lows from this year.
Although some correction is expected after such a significant move, analysts remain cautiously bullish at these levels.

"Indicators are moving into very overbought territory but they're not a worry yet. We have to watch for divergence in those indicators to indicate a downmove but there is no sign of that yet," said Chase's Stannard.
